message.content:
Here’s a quick example of how you can pull just the **IDs** and **context** fields for community comments from the `test4.org` domain, using the continuation cursor `cur456` and your API key `key123`.

---

## 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://api.yourservice.com/v1/communities/comments
```

> Replace `https://api.yourservice.com` with the actual base URL of the service you’re using.

---

## 2. Query Parameters

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `domain` | `test4.org` | The domain you’re querying. |
| `cursor` | `cur456` | The continuation cursor to fetch the next page. |
| `fields` | `id,context` | Tell the API to return only the `id` and `context` attributes. |
| `limit` | `50` (optional) | Number of items per page – adjust as needed. |

> **Tip:** If the API supports a `select` or `projection` syntax, use that instead of `fields`. The exact parameter name may vary.

---

## 3. Headers

```http
Authorization: Bearer key123
Accept: application/json
```

> Make sure the API key is passed as a bearer token (or whatever scheme the service requires).

---

## 4. Full Request Example (cURL)

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/communities/comments?domain=test4.org&cursor=cur456&fields=id,context" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

## 5. Expected Response

```json
{
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt001",
      "context": {
        "author": "alice",
        "timestamp": "2024-06-22T14:32:00Z",
        "text": "Great post!"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt002",
      "context": {
        "author": "bob",
        "timestamp": "2024-06-22T15:10:00Z",
        "text": "I agree with Alice."
      }
    }
    // …more comments
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // if there are more pages
}
```

> Only the `id` and `context` fields appear; all other comment metadata is omitted.

---

## 6. Handling Pagination

If the response contains a `next_cursor`, repeat the request with that cursor to fetch subsequent pages:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/communities/comments?domain=test4.org&cursor=cur789&fields=id,context" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Replace the base URL with your service’s endpoint.
- [ ] Verify the exact query‑parameter name for selecting fields (`fields`, `select`, etc.).
- [ ] Ensure the API key is correctly formatted in the `Authorization` header.
- [ ] Adjust `limit` if you need more or fewer items per request.

That’s it! Once you hit the endpoint with those parameters, you’ll get back only the IDs and context attributes for the community comments.
